items.status: Defined. Section variables are implicit: {need : U → Nat} {kids : U → List U} {use : U → Nat} {giving : Nat → Nat} {S : U → Prop} {hi : Nat}. `after` is defined as in the brief. `taken use w := total w use` (Becoming.total from Prelude), chosen so that SelectionTerm.Generations.sum matches it with no extra lemma. `left giving use w x := RegimeMargin.step giving (taken use w) x`. `Goes need s := ∃ u, u ∈ s.1 ∧ need u ≤ s.2`. `step := TurningInTime.pair (after need kids) (left giving use)`. `net := Law.stepWhile (Goes need) step`. `course := Law.orbit step s`. `allKids` is structural. `generation kids : Nat → List U → List U` (0 ↦ w, n+1 ↦ allKids kids (generation kids n w)). `lineTake S use w := total w fun u => if S u then use u else 0` and `lineCount S w := total w fun u => if S u then 1 else 0`, both taking [DecidablePred S]. `Goes` has a Decidable instance via `anyMet` (mirrors WayOfUnits.anyGoes).
theorems: def after (need : U → Nat) (kids : U → List U) : List U → Nat → List U | [], _ => [] | u :: w, x => cond (decide (need u ≤ x)) (kids u) [] ++ after need kids w x
def taken (use : U → Nat) (w : List U) : Nat := total w use
def lineTake (S : U → Prop) [DecidablePred S] (use : U → Nat) (w : List U) : Nat := total w fun u => if S u then use u else 0

items.item: 1. Who is in the next way; alike; lines reach each other only through the level
theorems:
theorem mem_after_iff {x : Nat} {v : U} :
    ∀ {w : List U}, v ∈ after need kids w x ↔ ∃ u, u ∈ w ∧ need u ≤ x ∧ v ∈ kids u

theorem after_alike {x x' : Nat} :
    ∀ {w : List U}, (∀ u, u ∈ w → (need u ≤ x ↔ need u ≤ x')) →
      after need kids w x = after need kids w x'

theorem after_append (x : Nat) :
    ∀ w₁ w₂ : List U, after need kids (w₁ ++ w₂) x = after need kids w₁ x ++ after need kids w₂ x

theorem taken_append (use : U → Nat) (w₁ w₂ : List U) :
    taken use (w₁ ++ w₂) = taken use w₁ + taken use w₂

theorem left_of_taken {giving : Nat → Nat} {use : U → Nat} {w₁ w₂ : List U} {x : Nat}
    (same : taken use w₁ = taken use w₂) : left giving use w₁ x = left giving use w₂ x
rests_on: local list lemmas mem_append_left/right/cases, append_assoc', mem_cond (written here, no core simp lemmas)

items.item: 2. Alike levels, one count, on any two stocks; the course as SelectionTerm.Generations
items.status: Proved, both halves. The Generations instance was cheap: `family_eq` follows by induction from `after_flatMap`, which holds by rfl at each cons.
theorems:
theorem way_generation {giving : Nat → Nat} {use : U → Nat} {w : List U} {x : Nat} :
    ∀ n, (∀ j, j < n → ∀ u, u ∈ generation kids j w →
        need u ≤ (course need kids giving use (w, x) j).2) →
      (course need kids giving use (w, x) n).1 = generation kids n w

theorem alike_one_count {g g' : Nat → Nat} {use use' : U → Nat} {w : List U} {x x' n : Nat}
    (met : ∀ j, j < n → ∀ u, u ∈ generation kids j w →
      need u ≤ (course need kids g use (w, x) j).2 ∧ need u ≤ (course need kids g' use' (w, x') j).2) :
    (course need kids g use (w, x) n).1 = generation kids n w ∧
      (course need kids g' use' (w, x') n).1 = generation kids n w

def generations (need : U → Nat) (kids : U → List U) (giving : Nat → Nat) (use : U → Nat)
    (s : List U × Nat) : SelectionTerm.Generations U where
  first := s.1
  kids t u := cond (decide (need u ≤ (course need kids giving use s t).2)) (kids u) []
  amount _ := use

theorem family_eq {giving : Nat → Nat} {use : U → Nat} (s : List U × Nat) :
    ∀ t, (generations need kids giving use s).family t = (course need kids giving use s t).1

theorem sum_eq {giving : Nat → Nat} {use : U → Nat} (s : List U × Nat) (t : Nat) :
    (generations need kids giving use s).sum t = taken use (course need kids giving use s t).1

theorem born_eq_length {giving : Nat → Nat} {use : U → Nat} (s : List U × Nat) (t : Nat) :
    SelectionTerm.born ((generations need kids giving use s).family t)
        ((generations need kids giving use s).kids t) =
      (course need kids giving use s (t + 1)).1.length

theorem after_unit : ∀ (w : List (Nat × Nat)) (x : Nat),
    after WayOfUnits.need (fun u => [u]) w x = WayOfUnits.after w x
theorem taken_unit : ∀ w : List (Nat × Nat), taken WayOfUnits.use w = WayOfUnits.taken w
theorem goes_unit (s : List (Nat × Nat) × Nat) : Goes WayOfUnits.need s ↔ WayOfUnits.Goes s

theorem step_unit (giving : Nat → Nat) (s : List (Nat × Nat) × Nat) :
    step WayOfUnits.need (fun u => [u]) giving WayOfUnits.use s =
      TurningInTime.pair WayOfUnits.after (WayOfUnits.left giving) s

theorem course_unit (giving : Nat → Nat) (s : List (Nat × Nat) × Nat) (n : Nat) :
    course WayOfUnits.need (fun u => [u]) giving WayOfUnits.use s n = WayOfUnits.course giving s n

theorem unending_unit (giving : Nat → Nat) (s : List (Nat × Nat) × Nat) :
    «不穷» (net WayOfUnits.need (fun u => [u]) giving WayOfUnits.use) «一» s ↔
      «不穷» (WayOfUnits.net giving) «一» s
rests_on: WayOfUnits.need, use, goes, after, taken, left, Goes, net, course (WayOfUnits)

items.status: Proved. The strong induction on m (`strong_below`, by induction on a bound) proves the claim `Ends ... hi m` from `ends_low` (x < m) and `ends_high` (m ≤ x, inner fuel induction with hi + 1 ≤ lineTake + k). The starting bound is m := total w need. The bound n ≤ hi + 2 in need_unmet holds as the brief wrote it.
theorems:
theorem line_ends [DecidablePred S] (nothing : RegimeMargin.FromNothing giving) (keeps : RegimeMargin.Keeps giving 0 hi)
    (same : ∀ u v, v ∈ kids u → (S v ↔ S u))
    (grows : ∀ u, S u → use u < lineTake S use (kids u)) (needs : ∀ u, S u → 0 < need u)
    (down : ∀ u v, S u → v ∈ kids u → need v ≤ need u) {w : List U} {x : Nat} (high : x ≤ hi) :
    ∃ n, ∀ k, n ≤ k → ∀ u, u ∈ (course need kids giving use (w, x) k).1 → ¬ S u

theorem way_ends {hi : Nat} (nothing : RegimeMargin.FromNothing giving)
    (keeps : RegimeMargin.Keeps giving 0 hi)
    (grows : ∀ u, use u < taken use (kids u)) (needs : ∀ u, 0 < need u)
    (down : ∀ u v, v ∈ kids u → need v ≤ need u) {w : List U} {x : Nat} (high : x ≤ hi) :
    (∃ n, ¬ Goes need (course need kids giving use (w, x) n)) ∧
      ¬ «不穷» (net need kids giving use) «一» (w, x)

theorem need_unmet {hi : Nat} (nothing : RegimeMargin.FromNothing giving)
    (keeps : RegimeMargin.Keeps giving 0 hi)
    (grows : ∀ u, use u < taken use (kids u)) (needs : ∀ u, 0 < need u)
    {w : List U} {x : Nat} (high : x ≤ hi) (ne : w ≠ []) (met : ∀ u, u ∈ w → need u ≤ x) :
    ∃ n, 0 < n ∧ n ≤ hi + 2 ∧ ∃ u, u ∈ (course need kids giving use (w, x) n).1 ∧
      (course need kids giving use (w, x) n).2 < need u

theorem keeps_any {giving : Nat → Nat} {hi : Nat} (keeps : RegimeMargin.Keeps giving 0 hi)
    (H x : Nat) (le : x ≤ hi) : RegimeMargin.step giving H x ≤ hi

changed_from_brief: `taken use w := total w use` (Prelude's total), not a new recursion. This makes SelectionTerm.Generations.sum equal to taken by congrArg alone. WayOfUnits.taken is shown equal to it by induction (taken_unit).
`generation` is defined with a structural `allKids` (kids u ++ allKids kids w), not with List.flatMap. `after_flatMap` links `after` to flatMap for the Generations family.

`lineTake` and `lineCount` are totals of `if S u then … else 0`, which needs [DecidablePred S]. The instance is an explicit argument only on the theorems that use lineTake or lineCount. A section instance variable would trip the unused-section-variable linter.

The item-6 corollary with S = fun _ => True is a separate theorem, `way_ends`. Its premises are stated without S: grows as `use u < taken use (kids u)`, and `down` without the `S u` premise. `lineTake_true` and `lineCount_true` link it to `line_ends`.

Helpers that are new here rather than taken from the package: local list lemmas (mem_append_*, append_assoc', mem_cond); `congr_two`, because core has no congrArg₂ under this toolchain; `step_falls`, `step_zero`, `keeps_any`, `course_fixed`, `unending_of_fixed`, `strong_below` and `orbit_congr`. I did not use core List or Nat simp lemmas, to keep the axiom report empty.
Item 8, 'a share that rises while the number of drawers falls': the line of C is given as `fun u => isC u = true`, with a Bool `isC`, so it is decidable without deriving DecidableEq.

Item 8, doubling and higher-start-from-seven: the configurations at the later steps (16 and 32 units) are given as length and level rather than the full list. Steps 0 to 4 from seven are given in full.
premises_not_needed: Rise (item 4) does not need `same`: `rise` and `draw_holds` hold for any predicate S with DecidablePred.
Item 2 (`way_generation`, `alike_one_count`, `family_eq`) needs no premise on giving, use or the start.
Item 7 (`taken_below`) needs no premise on kids, use or the start; only FromNothing and positive needs.
`need_unmet` needs no `down`, as the brief says, and no `same` (its line is every unit). It does use `needs`, `nothing`, `keeps`, `high`, `ne` and `met`; each is used in the proof.

In `line_ends` every listed premise is used: `nothing` and `needs` rule out the case of a draw above the level with the next level still ≥ m; `keeps` and `high` bound the levels; `same` and `down` carry Below to the next way.
not_done: Nothing in the brief's items 1 to 8 is left out.
